title: Ordered Pairs and the Cartesian Product
quickIdea: A x B is the set of ordered pairs with first coordinate from A and second from B. Order matters inside a pair, so A x B and B x A are different sets of the same size.
remember: A x B = {(a, b) : a in A and b in B}. The pair (a, b) is ordered: (a, b) = (c, d) exactly when a = c and b = d.
The cardinality is the product: |A x B| = |A| times |B|.
A x B and B x A have the same cardinality but are different sets unless A = B or one of them is empty.
The product with the empty set is empty: A x empty = empty, so the product has no elements even though the empty set is a set.
The product is not commutative but is associative up to the natural identification: (A x B) x C and A x (B x C) both consist of triples.
An ordered pair (a, b) is a set of sets, {a} and {a, b}, so a product lives inside P(P(A union B)). The construction is why a product can be built from the ZF axioms at all.
A relation from A to B is exactly a subset of A x B; a function from A to B is a relation in which every a in A appears exactly once as a first coordinate.
A subset of A x B need not be a product of a subset of A with a subset of B: the diagonal of a square is not a rectangle.
The number of elements of P(A x B) is 2 to the (|A| |B|), which is the number of relations from A to B.

example.prompt: A = {1, 2} and B = {a, b, c}. List A x B, give |A x B|, and say whether A x B = B x A.
example.work: Pair each element of A with each element of B: (1,a), (1,b), (1,c), (2,a), (2,b), (2,c). That is 2 times 3 = 6 pairs. B x A contains (a,1), which is not in A x B.
example.answer: |A x B| = 6, and A x B is not equal to B x A, although both have 6 elements.

gateAngle: GATE CS 1993 Q.8.4 is a product question in disguise: the power set of A x A has 2 to the (n squared) elements, which is also the number of relations on A.

variations.label: VERIFIED PYQ
variations.question: See GATE CS 1993 Q.8.4 in the linked PYQs of the power-set card: |A| = n, find the number of elements of P(A x A).
variations.why: The product A x A has n squared ordered pairs, and the power set of a set with k elements has 2 to the k.

variations.label: ORIGINAL PYQ-STYLE QUESTION
variations.question: A has 3 elements and B has 4. How many relations from A to B are there, and how many of them contain exactly one pair?
variations.answer: 2 to the 12 relations in total, and 12 of them contain exactly one pair.
variations.why: A relation is a subset of the 12-element product; the subsets of size 1 are the 12 singletons.

variations.label: PREDICTED VARIATION
variations.question: Is every subset of A x B of the form X x Y with X subset A and Y subset B?
variations.why: The diagonal {(1,1), (2,2)} of {1, 2} x {1, 2} is a subset that is not a product: any product containing (1,1) and (2,2) also contains (1,2).

trap.what: Treating the product as commutative, or assuming every subset of a product is a product.
trap.why: Ordered pairs remember which coordinate came first, and a product of subsets is a very special kind of subset - a rectangle in the grid picture.
trap.counterexample: A = B = {1, 2}. The subset {(1,2), (2,1)} is not a product X x Y: a product containing both pairs also contains (1,1) and (2,2).

check.question: |A| = 3, |B| = 4. How many elements does P(A x B) have?
check.explanation: The product has 12 elements, and the power set of a 12-element set has 2 to the 12 elements. This is also the number of relations from A to B.
